title: Advanced Architecture
subtopics: Separating domain logic from transport logic
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of advanced architecture in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to layered architecture.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers advanced architecture within advanced fastapi features and extensibility. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use advanced architecture to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is a small, well-defined behavior with explicit assumptions, a predictable result and a testable edge case.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Advanced Architecture matters because it is part of advanced fastapi features and extensibility. In practice, focus on a small, well-defined behavior with explicit assumptions, a predictable result and a testable edge case. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Separating domain logic from transport logic
items.text: For separating domain logic from transport logic, collect measurable evidence from a local or staging environment. Keep configuration environment-specific, avoid logging secrets, establish a rollback path, and do not claim performance or availability without measurements.

content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Layered architecture”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Advanced Architecture”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Layered architecture” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Advanced Architecture, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: Advanced Architecture belongs to the broader goal of a small, well-defined behavior with explicit assumptions, a predictable result and a testable edge case.
Use the source subtopics as the completeness checklist and verify expected results rather than relying on intuition.
Examples in this course are illustrative until technically reviewed and executed on a supported local environment.
